sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case M35: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 220x220x320 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case M35 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(220, 220, 320) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: myxoid soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 160/320 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: The image looks dark - let me check the sheet data.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to find edge marks that could define opposite corners of the tumor's bounding box, checking coordinates near the left, top, right, and bottom boundaries, but none of the existing marks line up cleanly as box corners.

Instead, I think using a single interior point on E34, which sits inside the tumor region, might be a simpler and more accurate approach.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 214.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 67–197, coronal 88–155, sagittal 105–168 | change +214.6 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 122, coronal 120, sagittal 137 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm trying to reconcile the coronal and sagittal views with the axial extent of the mask, since it seems to span from around slice 67 up to 197, with a tail-like extension near 162–178 that could be a separate vessel or lesion continuation rather than the main tumor body.

content.text: axial 165/320 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15
axial 180/320 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The upper region above 165 is ambiguous—the mask gets sloppy there, and it's unclear whether that intermediate-intensity tissue is a tumor tail extension or just normal bowel/muscle. I want to check the sagittal view at the center for more context, since the sagittal slice around 137 hinted at a thin upward extension, while the main tumor body spans roughly axial slices 67 to 160.

content.text: sagittal 137/220 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The sagittal display orientation is confusing me a bit, but working out the scale, the mask appears to span about 120mm, consistent with the axial extent of 67-197 (130mm). I also notice the mask boundary is fuzzy, and the tumor edge seems to extend slightly beyond the mask in some areas, particularly inferiorly.

Checking the clean images more carefully: there's a thin bright tail extending upward that looks like it could be a vessel or fascial band rather than tumor itself, so I'm tempted to trim the mask's upper boundary down to around axial slice 165-168. The axial slices in that region show irregular lobulated tissue near what might be iliac vessels or bowel, making it hard to tell where the tumor truly ends versus adjacent structures. I should check slices 150 and 158 to pin down the true inferior tumor boundary.

content.text: sheet axial 140–175/320 (6 slices) | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The tumor seems to top out around axial slice 163, with a flattened structure above it that's likely a vessel or bowel segment I need to erase from roughly slice 165 up to 200. I'm thinking of using a polygon-based paint erase over that slice range, which will require placing marks on an axial view to enclose the unwanted region.

content.text: axial 170/320 | crop full | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15 | fine marks appear in crops

content.thinking:
I notice at axial 170 there's additional tissue beyond the mask boundaries that isn't covered, possibly tumor extending cranially that wasn't fully captured. The tumor might have a tail-like extension along the vessels going up to around slice 190.

Let me check the coronal view at this location to better understand the anatomy, looking at the corresponding anterior-posterior slice to see how it relates to the mask center I identified earlier.

content.text: coronal 120/220 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Comparing the mask boundaries against the tumor extent in the coronal view, the mask seems to underestimate both the top and bottom edges of the tumor, so I'm converting the voxel coordinates to pixel measurements to check the scaling.

Looking at the top edge, the tumor rises on the patient-right side to about y~335 with a faint tail extending to y~310, matching the mask's hook shape there. I'm also trying to cross-reference the tissue seen at axial slices 165-180 with the coronal view — it looks like the same cranial continuation of the tumor, just viewed at a different scale factor (roughly 3.5 px/voxel in the axial view versus 2.4 px/voxel in the coronal), so I need to convert coordinates carefully before concluding they align.

Rather than keep reasoning through the index math, I think it's more reliable to just pull up the coronal slice near index 100 and crop around the mask to directly see the top boundary.

content.text: sheet coronal 90–150/220 (6 slices) | v1 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The coronal crop seems cut off oddly and isn't very helpful. I'm trying to get a clearer look at the axial slice around 168 to figure out the tumor's top boundary, which looks like it's around 163, with the thin sheet-like band above it (165-180) possibly being the parametrium or iliopsoas muscle.

The volume above 165 is small, maybe 5mL out of 215 total, so it's not critical either way, but I'll trim conservatively above 168 and focus more on refining the lower boundaries. To fix the top, I need to erase slices 166-200 using paint tools, which means I'll need to examine the mask crop carefully at slice 170 to place polygon marks that fully enclose the mask across all affected slices, since the mask spans a large area at 165.

content.text: axial 166/320 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The slice at 166 is too dark and the tissue shape looks irregular and broad, suggesting the tumor extends further than what the mask captured — it only grabbed an arc instead of the full extent. I'm considering adding a point in the unfilled interior tissue to help the model pick up that missing region, though contrast limitations make this tricky.

content.text: axial 166/320 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay none | v1 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The contrast here is too low to place reliable marks, unlike the earlier axial slice where edges were visible. I think I'll instead check the seg_candidates to see what's missing from the current segmentation.

content.text: v1 | no candidates: nothing next to the mask looks like it could belong to it | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I'm checking the coronal and sagittal slices to pin down which indices capture the tumor region, comparing extents across axes to figure out the right cropping boundaries.

content.text: sagittal 120/220 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The mask seems a bit tight but overall reasonable, though there's an upward tail of bright streaks at the top that the tumor blur extends into. Since the tissue around 166-180 is broad and similar in intensity to the tumor, but the sagittal view showed a thin tail there, I'd trim anything above 170 since that upper extent is likely not actual tumor.

That tail looks like a vessel-like linear structure running anteriorly rather than tumor itself. Since this contiguous volume is small, the effect on Dice either way is minor, so I'll just leave the mask through slice 175 and remove anything above 176, checking the edge marks on axial slice 180 to guide the trim — I still have plenty of budget left for this.

content.text: axial 178/320 | crop full | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I can't easily place marks near the tumor since the visible edges are far from it. Maybe a morphological opening with a small radius could strip away thin tail structures in the affected slices, since those sheets appear only a few voxels thick in-plane.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 211.7 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 69–178, coronal 88–155, sagittal 105–168 | change +0.0 mL / -2.9 mL | tool calls 19/40, prompts 1/15 | edit open | image: axial 121, coronal 120, sagittal 137 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: Checking the axial extent, which now spans 69-178, and noting the coronal hook near the top left persists along with a small notch at the upper body edge. The tumor's inferior boundary seems fuzzy and extends slightly beyond the mask boundary in both coronal and sagittal views, suggesting the segmentation might be cutting off some fading tumor tissue near the bottom.

content.text: sheet axial 50–90/320 (6 slices) | v2 | tool calls 20/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I notice the tumor's inferior extent at axial 74 is much larger than what the mask currently captures, while a fainter trace appears at axial 66 too. I should check slices 76 and 72 alongside the mask and place a positive point within the tumor region at slice 74 to correct the segmentation.

content.text: axial 74/320 | crop full | marks edges | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 21/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 74, I notice a bright blob around (230-350, 285-410) on the left panel that's more complex than the homogenous gray tumor seen at slice 80 — it has a dark curved cleft, suggesting it might be bowel like the cecum or ileum rather than the tumor's inferior pole, and the mask only covers part of it at this slice.

The real tumor at 74 likely spans the entire blob, with marks E11, E10, and E3 falling near its edges or interior. In the right panel coordinates, E11 sits at the left-edge interior while E10 is closer to center-right — I'll try using both as positive points, though there's some risk of leaking into adjacent bowel.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 242.3 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 58–191, coronal 87–155, sagittal 105–167 | change +31.5 mL / -0.8 mL | tool calls 22/40, prompts 2/15 | point add (2 mark(s)) | image: axial 121, coronal 120, sagittal 137 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The volume grew to 242 mL with extent now 58–191, and the upper boundary crept back up to 191, restoring that tail. I want to verify the coronal shape looks smooth at the top, so I'm checking the upper and lower slices around axial 56–80 and 160–195.

content.text: sheet axial 56–86/320 (6 slices) | v3 | tool calls 23/40, prompts 2/15
sheet axial 155–195/320 (6 slices) | v3 | tool calls 24/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
The mask now spans roughly 58 to 191, tapering toward the top. I'm checking the 171–187 region for whether that band is tumor or ambiguous tissue, and it seems to continue the tapering wedge shape, so I'll accept it up to about 185. Now I'm looking at the lower boundary around 62–68 to verify where the tumor edge actually starts.

I'm checking slice 62 near a small dark circular structure, likely a vessel or ureter, and confirming slice 56 shows nothing relevant. I also want to make sure normal structures like bowel aren't mistakenly included at slices 68 and 74, where the mask shows a triangular piece that looks questionable.

I'll do a final cross-check using coronal slice 100 and sagittal slice 150 on the cropped mask to confirm the boundaries hold up, then move to finish the segmentation review.

arguments.reason: Mask follows the tumor boundary in three planes; very low image contrast makes the superior and inferior tapering ends uncertain.

content.text: Final review of v3: volume 242.3 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 58–191, coronal 87–155, sagittal 105–167 | tool calls 25/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates: none found. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "8992" to save it.
The mask follows the tumor in all three planes and the end panels show no missed tumor, so I'm saving it.

arguments.reason: Single component outlining the ovoid T2-intermediate mass across all planes; end slices show no remaining tumor. Image contrast is very low, so the tapered superior tail and the inferior pole are uncertain.

content.text: case M35 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v3 | final volume 242.3 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 26/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the final mask for M35 at confidence medium. It is one connected component of 242.3 mL, spanning axial slices 58–191.

- **Main body:** the outline follows the oval T2-intermediate mass in axial, coronal and sagittal views. The end-of-mask review panels show no tumor left outside it. The automatic candidate check found nothing to add.
- **Inferior end:** the first mask under-covered the lower pole, so I added a second point there. That raised the volume from about 212 mL to 242 mL.
- **Superior tail:** the mass tapers upward into a thin band from about axial 165 to 191. I could not tell whether that band is tumor extension or normal tissue. I kept it, and it is a small share of the volume.
- **Image contrast:** the whole volume is very dark, so edges are blurry. That is why I did not rate the confidence higher.

I used 26 of 40 tool calls and 2 of 15 model prompts.
